# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.

bin/build
bin/start

I've written the acceptance test. Here's a summary.

## What I did

Added one new spec file: **`e2e/specs/invoice-notes.spec.ts`** — a faithful mirror of the existing `project-notes.spec.ts`, adapted to the invoice detail page. No existing spec needed changes: the request *adds* notes to invoices; it doesn't revise any behaviour the current suite asserts (projects keep their notes exactly as before, and no invoice spec asserted the absence of a notes region).

The spec has three tests, asserting **only through the UI (`data-testid`)** — this change records nothing to the audit file:

1. **Seeded display + newest-first + isolation** — three notes on invoice 1 seeded out of time order with ids that don't match time order, so the list can only pass if it sorts by `at` descending. Also seeds a note on invoice 2 *and* a note on project 1 (same numeric id, different `targetType`), asserting neither leaks in — proving notes are scoped by both `targetType` and `targetId`.
2. **Empty state** — an invoice with no notes shows `invoice-notes` + `invoice-notes-empty` and no note rows (casing-independent).
3. **Writing via the form** — an existing old note plus a newly written one, verifying the written note appears and sorts on top.

It uses the 3 new anchors (`invoice-notes`, `invoice-notes-empty`, `invoice-notes-list`) plus the shared, already-existing note anchors (`note-form`, `note-form-text`, `note-form-submit`, `note-row-<id>`, `note-text`), and reaches the invoice via `/invoices/<id>` — the same public URL surface `invoice-payments.spec.ts` uses.

## Verification

- **Fails for the right reason** against the pre-change app: all three tests get past `invoice-detail-page` (confirming seed + navigation are correctly arranged) and then fail only because the `invoice-notes` region doesn't exist yet. Exactly the expected pre-change state.
- I changed **no application source, build scripts, or seed helpers** — tests only.

## One thing worth flagging

Notes are polymorphic (`targetType`/`targetId`). I seed `targetType: 'INVOICE'` to match the codebase's uppercase enum convention (`SENT`/`DRAFT`/`ACTIVE`) and the sibling `project-notes.spec.ts` (which seeds `'PROJECT'`). 

While verifying, I noticed a **pre-existing inconsistency unrelated to my change**: on this build the notes *frontend* queries lowercase (`targetType=project`) while the seed path and the `project-notes` spec use uppercase `PROJECT`, and the GET endpoint matches case-sensitively — so 2 of the 3 existing `project-notes` tests currently fail on this build independently of anything I did. I left that spec untouched (the change request doesn't revise project-notes behaviour, and I write tests only). My invoice test follows the documented uppercase convention; whoever implements the invoice-notes feature should make uppercase-seeded invoice notes visible (the same contract the `project-notes` spec already defines for projects).
